desired_performances: Given a complex technical issue and a non-specialist audience, structure an explanation and adapt terminology to the audience.

No domain-specific technical background is assumed for the audience
success_criteria: Learner identifies at least two audience characteristics relevant to explanation adaptation
Learner articulates how each characteristic affects terminology or structure choices

assumption_notes: Audience analysis is treated as a prerequisite sub-skill for adaptation; this is a model candidate only and requires researcher validation

assessments.capability_claim: Learner can identify audience characteristics that should influence explanation strategy for a non-specialist audience.

required_evidence.criterion: At least two distinct audience characteristics (e.g., prior knowledge, role, goals) are explicitly identified from the scenario.
required_evidence.rationale: Corresponds to success criterion: identifies at least two relevant audience characteristics.

required_evidence.criterion: For each identified characteristic, the learner articulates a specific implication for terminology choice or explanation structure.
required_evidence.rationale: Corresponds to success criterion: articulates how each characteristic affects terminology or structure choices.

task.description: Read the provided scenario describing a technical issue and a non-specialist audience profile. Identify at least two audience characteristics and explain, for each, how it should influence the explanation strategy.
conditions: A written scenario describing a technical issue and a non-specialist audience profile is provided.
No domain-specific technical background is assumed for the audience.
Response is produced in writing without collaboration.

rubric_dimensions.criterion: Number and relevance of identified audience characteristics
performance_levels: Fewer than two characteristics identified, or characteristics are not relevant to explanation adaptation.
Two characteristics identified; relevance to explanation adaptation is implicit or partial.
Two or more characteristics identified; each is clearly relevant to explanation adaptation.

rubric_dimensions.criterion: Quality of articulated implication for each characteristic
performance_levels: No implication stated, or implication is generic and not linked to the specific characteristic.
Implication stated but connection to terminology or structure is vague.
Implication is specific and clearly linked to a terminology or structural choice.

scoring.mastery_rule: Candidate model: score at top level on both dimensions. Researcher must validate threshold.

assumption_notes: Scenario content and audience profile must be supplied by researcher; no factual content is generated here.
Rubric performance levels are candidate descriptors requiring researcher validation against the capability definition.

assessments.capability_claim: Learner can structure a written explanation of a complex technical issue in a logical sequence appropriate for a non-specialist reader.

required_evidence.criterion: The explanation follows an observable logical sequence (e.g., context is established before detail; problem is stated before solution).
required_evidence.rationale: Corresponds to success criterion: follows an observable logical sequence.

required_evidence.criterion: The structural sequence can be identified and evaluated without requiring domain expertise.
required_evidence.rationale: Corresponds to success criterion: structure is identifiable without domain expertise.

task.description: Given the specified technical topic and the non-specialist audience profile, produce a written explanation structured for that audience. Your response should make the logical sequence of your explanation discernible to a reader without domain expertise.
conditions: A defined technical topic is supplied.
Target audience is specified as non-specialist.
Learner produces a structured written explanation without collaboration.
No reference materials beyond the supplied topic description are permitted.

rubric_dimensions.criterion: Presence and observability of logical sequence
performance_levels: No discernible sequence; information is presented in an arbitrary or confusing order.
A partial sequence is present but transitions or ordering are inconsistent.
A clear logical sequence is present throughout and is observable without domain expertise.

rubric_dimensions.criterion: Appropriateness of sequence for a non-specialist reader
performance_levels: Sequence assumes specialist background or omits necessary context.
Sequence is broadly appropriate but includes isolated assumptions of prior knowledge.
Sequence consistently places context and framing before detail, appropriate for a non-specialist.

scoring.mastery_rule: Candidate model: top level on both dimensions. 'Logical sequence' definition must be validated by researcher against the capability definition before use.

assumption_notes: 'Logical sequence' is not defined in the brief; the rubric operationalisation here is a model candidate and requires researcher validation.
Prerequisite reference to lo-tc-01 is a model-proposed candidate only.
Topic and audience profile must be supplied by researcher.

assessments.capability_claim: Learner can adapt a specialist-audience explanation by replacing or defining specialist terminology to be accessible to a specified non-specialist audience without introducing factual inaccuracies.

required_evidence.criterion: Specialist terms present in the source are replaced with plain-language alternatives or accompanied by definitions accessible to the specified audience.
required_evidence.rationale: Corresponds to success criterion: specialist terms are replaced or defined in plain language.

required_evidence.criterion: No factual inaccuracies are introduced in the adapted explanation, as determined by a domain-informed evaluator.
required_evidence.rationale: Corresponds to success criterion: adapted explanation does not introduce factual inaccuracies.

required_evidence.criterion: The revised explanation is self-contained and assessable without access to the original specialist source.
required_evidence.rationale: Corresponds to success criterion: revised text is assessable without the original source.

task.description: You are provided with a written explanation of a technical topic intended for a specialist audience and a profile of a non-specialist audience. Produce a revised version of the explanation that is accessible to the specified non-specialist audience. Your revised version must be self-contained.
conditions: A source explanation containing specialist terminology is provided.
A non-specialist audience profile is specified.
Learner produces a revised written explanation without collaboration.
The revised explanation must be evaluable without reference to the original source.

performance_levels: Specialist terms are largely retained without definition or accessible replacement.
Most specialist terms are addressed but one or more significant terms remain inaccessible.
All identified specialist terms are replaced with plain-language alternatives or clearly defined.

rubric_dimensions.criterion: Factual accuracy of the adapted explanation (domain-informed evaluator required)
performance_levels: Adaptation introduces one or more factual inaccuracies.
No clear inaccuracies but meaning is distorted or oversimplified to the point of misleading.
Adapted explanation is factually accurate as judged by a domain-informed evaluator.
Revised explanation requires access to the original source to be understood or evaluated.
Revised explanation is mostly self-contained but contains isolated references requiring the source.
Revised explanation is fully self-contained and assessable without the original source.

scoring.mastery_rule: Candidate model: top level on all three dimensions. Dimension rd-tc-03-2 requires a domain-informed human evaluator; automated scoring is not specified. Researcher must validate before operational use.

assumption_notes: Factual accuracy evaluation (ev-tc-03-b, rd-tc-03-2) requires a domain-informed human evaluator; this cannot be automated without additional specification.

Source explanation and audience profile must be supplied by researcher; no factual content is generated here.
60-minute constraint noted; three assessments are proposed as a candidate scope — feasibility within the time constraint must be confirmed by researcher.

prerequisites.capability: Learner can read and comprehend a written scenario or description of a technical issue at a general adult literacy level.
prerequisites.rationale: All three assessments require reading a supplied written scenario or source text; basic reading comprehension is an implicit entry condition for any written-analysis or text-adaptation task.

prerequisites.capability: Learner has a working concept of 'audience' as a factor that influences how a message is composed (i.e., that the same information may be expressed differently for different readers).
prerequisites.rationale: lo-tc-01 asks learners to analyze audience characteristics and derive implications for explanation strategy; this requires an existing mental model of audience as a variable in communication, not just a destination.

prerequisites.capability: Learner can distinguish between specialist and non-specialist vocabulary in a given text (i.e., can flag terms likely to be unfamiliar to a general reader).
prerequisites.rationale: lo-tc-03 requires replacing or defining specialist terminology; the learner must first be able to identify which terms qualify as specialist relative to a specified audience before adapting them.

prerequisites.capability: Learner can produce a coherent multi-sentence written response in English.
prerequisites.rationale: All summative tasks require written production (written-analysis, structured-written-explanation, text-adaptation); the ability to compose connected prose in the assessment language is a prerequisite for demonstrating any of the target capabilities.

prerequisites.capability: Learner understands the concept of logical sequence in expository writing (e.g., that context or problem statement can precede detail or solution).
prerequisites.rationale: lo-tc-02 requires applying a logical sequence appropriate for a non-specialist reader; awareness that expository texts can be ordered in principled ways is a candidate entry condition before the learner can make deliberate structural choices.
